key_patterns.name: Layered social influence
key_patterns.description: Family, work/school, and community layers provide different contact intensities and likely different influence strengths on adoption.
key_patterns.relevance: Set layer-specific interaction frequencies and social influence weights to reproduce observed adoption curves and subgroup disparities.

key_patterns.name: Risk-driven propensity
key_patterns.description: Higher risk_perception is expected to correlate with higher baseline adoption and lower social threshold for adoption.
key_patterns.relevance: Use risk_perception to initialize agent propensities and to parameterize adoption thresholds or utility coefficients.

key_patterns.name: Homophily by age and occupation
key_patterns.description: Connections cluster within the same age_group and occupation (especially students in school networks and co-workers in work/school layer).
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily amplifies local norm cascades; calibrate mixing matrices and layer-specific degree distributions to capture diffusion speed and clustering effects.

key_patterns.name: Persistence of mask-wearing
key_patterns.description: Once adopted, wearing_mask tends to persist across days with rare reversals, unless data show policy or norm shocks.
key_patterns.relevance: High persistence reduces volatility; calibrate abandonment rates to match observed persistence and peak adoption magnitude.

key_patterns.name: Information precedes adoption
key_patterns.description: received_info tends to increase before or concurrently with surges in wearing_mask; adoption hazard is higher when informed.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports a two-process model: information diffusion followed by behavior adoption; calibrate these processes separately.

key_patterns.name: Temporal lag between info and adoption
key_patterns.description: A short lag (1–5 days) is often seen between spikes in received_info and subsequent adoption increases.
key_patterns.relevance: Include a lagged effect of information on adoption hazard to reproduce timing of TimeTo50Percent and PeakAdoption.

key_patterns.name: Directed or inconsistent edges in network JSON
key_patterns.description: Adjacency lists may not be reciprocated and can include duplicates or self-loops.
key_patterns.relevance: Preprocessing (symmetrization, deduplication) is needed for consistent influence calculations and degree metrics.

key_patterns.name: Subgroup adoption disparities
key_patterns.description: Adoption rates likely differ across age_group and occupation, and across risk_perception terciles.
key_patterns.relevance: Targets for SubgroupDisparityIndex; informs group-specific parameters (e.g., susceptibility, thresholds, or contact rates).

key_distributions.name: Risk perception distribution
key_distributions.description: risk_perception ∈ [0,1]; typically right-skewed or bimodal depending on population.
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Beta(a,b) to the empirical risk_perception; store a,b for agent initialization.

key_distributions.name: Degree distributions by layer
key_distributions.description: Family layer low mean degree with high clustering; work/school moderate to high; community more dispersed/heavy-tailed.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L ∈ {family, work_school, community}: mean degree μ_L, variance σ²_L, quantiles (p10, p50, p90), clustering coefficient C_L.

key_distributions.name: Initial states
key_distributions.description: Day 0 proportions for wearing_mask and received_info.
key_distributions.parameters: p_mask0 = P(wearing_mask=1 | day=0); p_info0 = P(received_info=1 | day=0).

key_distributions.name: Information diffusion hazard
key_distributions.description: Daily probability of becoming informed among the uninformed.
key_distributions.parameters: λ_info(t) = P(received_info_t=1 | received_info_{t−1}=0); optionally stratified by layer exposure and subgroups.

key_distributions.name: Adoption hazards
key_distributions.description: Daily probability of adopting among non-wearers, conditional on info and social exposure.
key_distributions.parameters: λ_adopt_info(t) = P(wearing_mask_t=1 | wearing_mask_{t−1}=0, received_info_t=1); λ_adopt_noinfo(t) similarly; include peer adoption fraction as covariate.

key_distributions.name: Persistence/abandonment
key_distributions.description: Probability of continuing to wear once adopted; abandonment is 1−persistence.

key_distributions.name: Adoption timing
key_distributions.description: Distribution of time-to-adoption among eventual adopters.
key_distributions.parameters: Survival curve S(t); median time-to-adoption; hazard ratios by subgroup.

key_relationships.relationship: Monotonic positive: higher risk_perception increases baseline log-odds of adoption and lowers thresholds.
key_relationships.strength: To estimate via logistic hazard; expect moderate to strong.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive social contagion; marginal effect likely strongest in family, then work/school, then community.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate layer-specific coefficients β_family > β_work_school > β_community.
Typically strong; quantify as odds ratio > 1.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher degree increases exposure and info hazard, especially in high-intensity layers.
Group fixed effects capturing norms/policies (e.g., students may adopt earlier due to school mandates).

symmetrize_edges.value: Undirected symmetrization per layer; keep edge if i->j or j->i
symmetrize_edges.notes: Deduplicate and remove self-loops; maintain separate edge sets per layer.

contact_rate_by_layer.value: c_family, c_work_school, c_community computed from degree and scheduling (e.g., daily family and work; community sampled stochastically)
contact_rate_by_layer.notes: Scale such that expected daily contacts reflect empirical degrees; optionally cap community contacts.

layer_influence_weights.value: w_family > w_work_school > w_community (estimate via regression on adoption hazard)
layer_influence_weights.notes: Normalize weights to sum to 1 for interpretability.

homophily_indices.value: Assortativity coefficients r_age, r_occupation per layer
homophily_indices.notes: Use as calibration targets to ensure network mixing is preserved.

risk_perception_distribution.notes: Store fitted a,b; use to sample agents if simulating synthetic populations.

initial_mask_rate_day0.notes: Seed initial adopters by sampling agents to match group-specific rates if available.

initial_info_rate_day0.notes: Initialize informed state consistent with data.

baseline_propensity_function.value: logit(p0_i) = α0 + α_r * risk_perception_i + α_age[age_group] + α_occ[occupation]
baseline_propensity_function.notes: Fit α’s to match day0 cross-sectional adoption by subgroups.

info_hazard_baseline.notes: Estimate overall discrete-time hazard; stratify if non-stationary.

info_transmission_prob_by_layer.value: {p_info_family, p_info_work_school, p_info_community} from regression of new info events on informed neighbors by layer
info_transmission_prob_by_layer.notes: Fit discrete-time contagion model with exposure counts or fractions.

info_effect_lag_days.value: L_info→adopt ∈ [0,5], chosen to maximize fit to adoption timing
info_effect_lag_days.notes: Select via grid search on lag minimizing RMSE of adoption series.

social_influence_coefficients.value: {β_family, β_work_school, β_community} on fraction of neighbors wearing at t−1
social_influence_coefficients.notes: Estimate via logistic hazard among non-wearers; include info and risk controls.

risk_sensitivity_coefficient.value: β_risk on risk_perception in adoption hazard
risk_sensitivity_coefficient.notes: Positive coefficient expected; calibrate to subgroup gradients.

spontaneous_adoption_rate.value: λ_spont = P(wear_t=1 | wear_{t−1}=0, received_info_t=0, no exposed neighbors)
spontaneous_adoption_rate.notes: Captures media or exogenous adoption pressure.

persistence_probability.notes: Set abandonment_rate = 1 − p_persist; allow time-variation if policy changes observed.

threshold_distribution.value: τ_i = max(0, min(1, 1 − γ * risk_perception_i + ε_i)), ε_i ~ N(0, σ²_τ)
threshold_distribution.notes: For threshold-based models; calibrate γ and σ²_τ against adoption timing and peak.

interaction_schedule.value: Daily family and work/school interactions; community interactions sampled with probability p_comm_day
interaction_schedule.notes: Tune p_comm_day to match info/adoption hazards.

adoption_series_targets.value: Match daily population adoption series; compute RMSE, MAE, MAPE, R2

subgroup_disparity_targets.value: Adoption gaps/ratios across age_group, occupation, and risk_perception terciles
subgroup_disparity_targets.notes: Use as multi-objective penalties to preserve heterogeneity.

run_to_run_variance_target.value: Variance of adoption at evaluation day T across ≥30 replications
run_to_run_variance_target.notes: Set acceptable variance band based on empirical day-to-day variability.

preprocessing_steps.step: Validate agent_id integrity and join keys
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure all agent_ids are unique in agent_attributes and present in network and time series.
Cast IDs to int, remove self-loops, deduplicate neighbors, and symmetrize edges per layer.

preprocessing_steps.step: Compute layer-wise degree and clustering metrics
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Summarize network structure for parameterization and to use as calibration targets.
Check monotonicity per agent; if non-decreasing, treat as cumulative; else treat as daily event and construct cumulative if needed.
For each agent-day, compute fraction of neighbors wearing by layer; needed for hazard regressions.
Estimate info hazard, adoption hazards (with/without info), and persistence from transitions in the time series.
Compute subgroup-specific adoption and information rates to calibrate disparity indices.
Hold out the last K days (e.g., 20%) or a subset of subgroups for out-of-sample validation.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a staged, multi-objective calibration. Stage 1: Fit statistical models to extract direct parameters. (a) Fit Beta(a,b) to risk_perception. (b) Estimate info diffusion via discrete-time hazard models: logit P(info_t=1 | not informed) = θ0 + Σ_L θ_L * exposure_info_L(t−1) + group FE. (c) Estimate adoption hazard among non-wearers: logit P(wear_t=1) = β0 + β_info * received_info_{t−L} + Σ_L β_L * peer_frac_L(t−1) + β_risk * risk_perception + age/occ FE. Stage 2: Map coefficients to simulation parameters (layer weights, risk sensitivity, spontaneous adoption). Stage 3: Run simulation and perform simulation-based optimization (e.g., Bayesian optimization or SMC/ABC) to minimize a weighted loss across RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and to match timing (TimeTo50Percent, PeakAdoption) and subgroup disparities. Include penalties if RunToRunVariance exceeds empirical variability. Iterate until convergence of metrics on calibration set.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Evaluate on held-out days and/or subgroups. Compute RMSE, MAE, MAPE, R2 for the adoption time series; compare TimeTo50Percent and PeakAdoption timing. Assess SubgroupDisparityIndex across age_group, occupation, and risk_perception terciles. Run ≥30 stochastic replications to estimate RunToRunVariance at evaluation day T and at peak; ensure intervals cover observed adoption with appropriate width. Perform sensitivity analysis on key parameters (β_risk, β_L, p_persist) and check robustness. Conduct posterior predictive checks: trajectory shapes, plateau levels, and response to changes in received_info.
key_variables_to_calibrate: threshold parameters (γ, σ²_τ) if using threshold model
baseline_propensity intercepts and group fixed effects (α0, α_age, α_occ)

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Overall structure and type
  - File type: flat CSV; one row per agent (no nesting).
  - Columns/data types:
    - agent_id: integer, unique primary key.
    - age_group: categorical string (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age).
    - occupation: categorical string (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar).
    - risk_perception: float in [0,1], continuous.

- Meaning of keys/columns
  - agent_id: stable identifier to instantiate agents and to join with other datasets (e.g., network edges, households).
  - age_group: life-stage category influencing social contexts (school vs work), homophily, and baseline compliance norms.
  - occupation: role affecting daily contact settings (school, workplace type), peer groups, and norm environments.
  - risk_perception: agent’s baseline subjective perception of health risk; higher values imply greater intrinsic propensity to wear masks and/or lower threshold for adoption.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - No nested structures; each row is independent.
  - Implicit relationships:
    - age_group and occupation inform likely interaction layers (e.g., Students → school network; Blue/White Collar → workplace clusters).
    - agent_id serves as foreign key to external network/household/contact data.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Agent initialization:
    - Create an Agent for each row with attributes: {age_group, occupation, risk_perception}.
    - Set initial mask-wearing propensity p0 via a function of risk_perception and optionally age/occupation (e.g., logistic model).
  - Network formation/mixing:
    - Use age_group and occupation to construct or weight edges: homophily within age/occupation; context-specific layers (household, school, workplace, community).
    - Determine contact rates by context (e.g., Students higher school-layer contacts).
  - Behavior dynamics:
    - Adoption rule parameters:
      - Threshold models: personal threshold τ_i could be 1 − risk_perception (higher risk → lower required peer adoption).
      - Utility/logit models: include risk_perception as a positive coefficient; age/occupation as fixed effects.
      - Influence susceptibility: weight social signals differently by occupation/age (e.g., students more peer-sensitive).
    - Norm propagation:
      - Occupation and age_group can set context-specific norms and conformity pressure on edges within those contexts.
  - Calibration/validation:
    - Ensure agent_id uniqueness; risk_perception ∈ [0,1].
    - Use observed distributions to match desired population heterogeneity in the simulation.

- Overall data structure and type:
  - JSON object representing a multiplex social network as adjacency lists.
  - Top-level: mapping from agent ID (stringified integer) to a dictionary of relationship layers.
- Meaning of keys:
  - Top-level keys ("0", "1", …): unique agent identifiers.
  - Nested keys: "family", "work_school", "community" denote distinct social layers.
  - Values of each nested key: list of agent IDs (integers) that the focal agent is connected to in that layer.
- Relationships and nested elements:
  - Each agent has up to three neighbor lists, one per layer.
  - Edges are encoded from the perspective of the focal agent; reciprocity is not guaranteed (i.e., the graph may be directed unless symmetrized).
  - No weights, timestamps, or attributes are provided; lists imply unweighted ties. Potential overlaps across layers may exist.
  - IDs in lists should correspond to existing agents; verify and handle missing references, duplicates, or self-loops if present.
- How this should inform simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agents: one agent per top-level key; initialize behavioral state (e.g., mask-wearing), propensity, and other attributes externally since not provided here.
  - Network model: construct a three-layer (multiplex) graph with separate edge sets for family, work/school, and community.
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Use layer-specific contact frequencies and influence strengths (e.g., family > work/school > community) to model exposure to mask-wearing norms.
    - At each time step, sample interactions within each layer according to its intensity; compute influence from neighbors on adoption/abandonment.
    - Decide whether to treat edges as undirected (by symmetrizing) or directed (as-is) and be consistent across layers.
  - Calibration hooks: assign per-layer transmission/influence probabilities, scheduling (daily work/school vs. occasional community), and thresholds or contagion rules.
  - Validation: ensure all referenced IDs exist; cast string IDs to integers or maintain a consistent mapping; de-duplicate neighbor lists if needed.

- Data structure and type:
  - CSV file in tidy, longitudinal (panel) format.
  - One record per agent per day; composite primary key is (day, agent_id).
  - Data types: day (integer), agent_id (integer), wearing_mask (boolean), received_info (boolean).

- Meaning of columns:
  - day: Discrete simulation timestep, starting at 0.
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for an agent.
  - wearing_mask: Agent’s mask-wearing state on that day (adoption state).
  - received_info: Whether the agent has received pro-mask information on that day (information exposure state/event). Clarify in data: is this “ever informed by or before day t” (cumulative) or “informed today” (daily event); check monotonicity across days to decide.

- Relationships or nested elements:
  - No nested structures; flat rows.
  - Temporal dependency within agent: state at day t can depend on state at day t−1 (Markov-style transitions).
  - No social network topology provided here; any neighbor-based effects must come from another source or be assumed.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions:
  - Agent schema: {id, wearing_mask, informed(received_info)} initialized from day 0.
  - Calibrate/update rules:
    - Estimate transition probabilities from sequences:
      - P(received_info_t=1 | received_info_{t−1}=0) = information spread baseline (or use with network data if available).
      - P(wearing_mask_t=1 | wearing_mask_{t−1}=0, received_info_t=1) = adoption given info.
      - P(wearing_mask_t=1 | wearing_mask_{t−1}=0, received_info_t=0) = spontaneous adoption.
      - Persistence P(wearing_mask_t=1 | wearing_mask_{t−1}=1).
  - Interaction logic:
    - If network data are available, propagate received_info via edges with probability calibrated above; otherwise use global/contact-rate assumptions.
    - Adoption dynamics use received_info as a driver; once informed/adopted, states typically persist (unless data show reversals).
  - Validation targets:
    - Match time series of proportions informed and wearing masks; agent-level transition rates.
